channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Genome Biology, Genome Research, and Molecular Cell.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Reinvigorating COTL1 high NK cells via GITR signalling overcomes immune checkpoint blockade resistance in tsMHC-I-impaired tumours
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 30 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01925-9 You, Hu et al. discover a population of COTL1high NK cells regulated by GITRL+ macrophages and demonstrate their functional importance in mediating anti-tumour immunity in cancer with impaired tumour-specific MHC-I expression.

item.title: Genome Biology: Predicting extinction risk of gibbons from genomes of extinct Yunnan lar gibbon

Genome Biology: EMF2b-1 regulates endosperm cell cycling through PRC2 recruitment in maize
Nature Cell Biology: An EGFR co-amplified lncRNA HELDR promotes glioblastoma malignancy through KAT7-driven gene programs
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 27 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01924-w Yu et al. identify HELDR as a lncRNA co-amplified with EGFR in glioblastoma to promote a KAT7-activated malignancy programme, which can be potentially targeted with anti-EGFR therapy for improved therapeutic outcomes.

item.title: Genome Biology: Functional characterization of transporter genes in rice node at single-cell resolution through multi-omics technologies
Molecular Cell: The Erlin1/2 complex is a dynamic scaffold for membrane microdomain assembly on the endoplasmic reticulum
item.description: Yan et al. reveal the structure of the ER-resident Erlin1/2 complex, showing how it assembles into a cage-like architecture that organizes functional membrane microdomains on the ER membrane and regulates cargo protein accessibility. These findings provide a structural framework for understanding Erlin-mediated processes on the ER membrane.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Nonsense-mediated mRNA decay safeguards telomeres in pluripotent stem cells
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 24 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01912-0 Markiewicz-Potoczny et al. report that the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay pathway protects telomeres in the absence of core Shelterin component TRF2 by regulating the stability and abundance of TRF1 at telomeres.

item.title: Genome Biology: Dynamic changes in Lamin B1 and heterochromatin coincide with chromatin condensation during human erythropoiesis
Genome Biology: ER tethering and active transport govern condensate diffusion during hyperosmotic stress
Molecular Cell: A cytomegalovirus-encoded lncRNA blocks cell-cycle progression
item.description: Human cytomegalovirus expresses the highly abundant lncRNA RNA2.7 to reprogram host gene expression. RNA2.7 stabilizes cellular mRNAs by sequestering RNA-binding proteins and enforces a G1-S cell-cycle arrest specifically in actively cycling cells through an adenosine-rich region, thereby promoting efficient viral replication.

item.title: Genome Biology: A kingdom-wide full-length RNA atlas reveals the evolutionary landscapes of plant poly(A) tails
Genome Biology: Co-occurrence of rare variants implicates gene pairs in cytoskeletal pathways and is associated with increased severity in autism spectrum disorder
Molecular Cell: NAC promotes co-translational protein folding at the ribosomal tunnel exit
item.description: Santos et al. reveal NAC’s co-translational interactome, showing compartment-specific nascent chain interactions in human cells. NAC engages emerging chains at the ribosomal tunnel exit via a ribosome-oriented hydrophobic pocket, promoting early domain folding without stabilizing intermediate structures. These findings establish NAC as a co-translational chaperone integrating folding with protein biogenesis.

item.title: Molecular Cell: RNF25 confers mRNA damage tolerance by curbing activation of the integrated stress response
item.description: Zhao et al. show that azacytidine-induced cytotoxicity is primarily mediated by its incorporation into mRNA. This triggers detrimental activation of the integrated stress response, which is restrained by the ubiquitin ligase RNF25, revealing RNA damage as a central component of azacytidine treatment and identifying an mRNA-damage tolerance pathway.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Visualizing suborganellar lipid distribution using correlative light and electron microscopy
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 20 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01915-x Lennartz et al. introduce a correlative light and electron microscopy workflow, Lipid-CLEM, combining near-native lipid probes and on-section labelling via click chemistry. Lipid-CLEM quantitatively analyses lipids in membrane nanodomains.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Replicative gaps in DNA damage tolerance, genome instability, and cancer therapy
item.description: Replicative single-stranded DNA gaps arise when DNA synthesis proceeds past lesions or difficult-to-replicate regions. This review delineates the pathways that generate, stabilize, and process these intermediates and discusses how their persistence drives fork degradation, genome instability, innate immune activation, and altered responses to DNA damage response-targeted therapies.

item.title: Genome Biology: Phase separation of β-catenin assembles active loop hubs in colorectal cancer
Genome Biology: Sex chromosome evolution mediated by a large inversion and a possible switch of the sex determination gene
Molecular Cell: LENG8 mediates RNA nuclear retention and degradation in eukaryotes
item.description: Tian et al. identify LENG8 as a conserved RNA quality-control factor that prevents nuclear export of misprocessed mRNAs and noncoding RNAs. This study provides fundamental insight into how the surveillance machinery monitors RNA processing status to determine nuclear retention, degradation, or export.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Paraspeckle condensation is controlled via TDP-43 polymerization and linked to neuroprotection
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 18 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01895-y Hodgson, Huang, Lang et al. show that TDP-43 limits ribonucleoprotein particle condensation into paraspeckles in a concentration- and polymerization-dependent manner. They also link paraspeckle condensation to stress response and neuroprotection.

Genome Biology: Centromere evolution in annual and perennial soybeans and its implication for hybridization in cultivated species
Molecular Cell: Microhomology-mediated end joining acts directly on replication forks to repair single-ended double-strand breaks
item.description: Li et al. uncover a new mechanism, fork-MMEJ, at broken replication forks that repairs seDSBs with characteristics distinct from the canonical MMEJ (cMMEJ). This study provides insights into replication-associated DSB repair, implicates microhomology-mediated chromosomal rearrangements in cancer, and offers potential therapeutic strategies to selectively target cancer cells.

item.title: Genome Biology: Systematic evaluation of single-cell multimodal data integration enhances cell type resolution and discovery of clinically relevant states in complex tissues
Molecular Cell: Molecular basis for dual-spacer-guided target cleavage by the TIGR-TasH system
item.description: Yang et al. presented the molecular basis of the TIGR-TasH system, including autonomous precursor tigRNA processing by the Nop domain, tigRNA-dependent dimerization, lysine-triggered dsDNA unzipping, and β-hairpin-mediated recruitment of the HNH nuclease. Engineering Box C mutants enable the rational design of tigRNA-defined nickases for gene editing in mammalian cells.
